stage_2_story.text_en:
Every Saturday morning, Moshe stops at a small café near his house before going to the market. The café is always busy on weekends, so there is usually a long queue by the entrance. Moshe does not mind waiting because he enjoys watching the barista work — the young man moves quickly and makes every coffee look like a work of art.

When it is Moshe's turn, he orders his usual: a large cappuccino with an extra shot of espresso and no syrup. He has been coming here for three years, so the barista already knows his order. Moshe also picks up a warm pastry — usually an almond croissant — to eat at the small table by the window.

He pulls out his loyalty card and hands it over. Today is the tenth stamp, which means his coffee is free. He smiles and feels like he has won a small prize.

Moshe does not like to rush on Saturday mornings. He sits for twenty minutes, drinks his coffee slowly, and reads the news on his phone. The foam on top of the cappuccino is thick and sweet. He thinks about ordering a takeaway next week so he can drink it in the park, but then he decides — no, sitting here is the best part of his weekend.
